title: It Looks Nice, but the Tray is Too Small
text:
It Looks Nice, but the Tray is Too Small. Like most families, ours has a dishwasher but regardless, we still wash some dishes by hand. It could be because the dishwasher is already full or it could be because some items are better cleaned when washed by hand. Whatever the reason, hand washing is not likely to go away and that fact coupled with the need for a quality means for drip drying dishes led me to get the Homelody Dish Rack.

Straight from the box, this dish rack does look nice and its shiny stainless steel construction is one of its best qualities. It comes with separate attachments for glasses and for silverware that you can attach where you like. And since the four glass/cup holders keep the cups on the outside of the rack, there is more room on the inside for other dishes.

Homelody Dish Rack holds a good amount of dishes and I like the way it looks. But there is one problem with this dish rack that I cannot overlook and that is with the drainage tray. The tray is not large enough to capture all of the drips and anything on the edges- like cups- are going to drip water all over your counter top. You need to have a towel underneath the rack or another, larger tray, to catch these drips.

There is one other issue I have with the tray that makes it less convenient, and that is the simple fact that the tray is closed on all sides. With other dish racks, the tray is slanted in one direction with an open end that you can place right over your sink so that the water drains into the sink. There is no such feature like that with this Homelody Dish Rack. You have to periodically lift it up and pour the water down the drain.

As I said, I do like the appearance of this dish rack and it looks great in my kitchen, which is already accented with stainless steel appliances. But the issues with the drip tray are a concern and I’m not so sure I am willing to completely give up my old dish rack for this reason. I might have to shop for and purchase a large, sloping tray and use it instead. That might be enough to convince me to give this dish rack a permanent home on my kitchen counter top. But until that happens, I plan on only limited use for this dish rack and can only rate it average overall for the reasons stated above.
